hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try only the first part: when $x = 3$, what is $x^2$? Remember that it means $3 \times 3$.
This expression has two parts that both use $x$. Find the value of each part before adding.
With $x = 3$, the parts are $3^2$ and $2(3)$. Work out the power and the product, then add them.
$3^2 = 9$ and $2 \times 3 = 6$, and $9 + 6 = 15$, so the value is $15$.

explanation: Put $3$ in place of every $x$, which gives $3^2 + 2(3)$.
Exponents come first in the order of operations: $3^2 = 3 \times 3 = 9$.
Next do the multiplication in the second term: $2 \times 3 = 6$.
Add the two parts: $9 + 6 = 15$. The value is $15$.
